question: Where does the urinary bladder sit in relation to the uterus in females?

options.A: Lateral to the right and left ovaries
options.B: Directly posterior to the rectal wall
options.C: Posterior and superior to the uterus
options.D: Anterior and inferior to the uterus

explanation: In simple terms, your bladder sits right in front of (anterior) and lower down (inferior) than your uterus. That's why pregnancy puts so much direct squeeze on the bladder! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h7)

question: How does heparin mainly work in the body?

options.A: By activating antithrombin III
options.B: By binding directly to blood platelets
options.C: By blocking calcium ion absorption
options.D: By depleting dietary vitamin K

explanation: Heparin teams up with a helper in your blood called antithrombin III to quickly put the brakes on clotting factors. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h2)

question: What key message should form the heart of community health campaigns against abusive widowhood rites?

options.A: Honoring the dead should never involve harming or degrading the living
options.B: Widows should relocate to foreign countries immediately after a loss
options.C: All traditional cultural practices in Africa must be completely abolished
options.D: Men should be subjected to the exact same mourning rituals

explanation: Focusing the message on respect for human life and dignity wins people over while clearly standing against dangerous rituals. Fantastic job completing this set! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T10#GNS225_U6_T10_h7)

question: Why should young adult men learn to do regular testicular self-examinations?

options.A: It helps detect lumps or changes early when treatment is most effective
options.B: It stops the development of benign prostatic hyperplasia later in life
options.C: It guarantees complete protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: It prevents the normal age-related decline in testosterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! Just like breast self-exams for women, checking early helps catch unusual lumps or changes when treatment works best. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h7)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial check to perform on a direct laryngoscope before the procedure starts?

options.A: Testing the light source to ensure the bulb works
options.B: Filling the battery compartment with sterile water
options.C: Calibrating the internal digital video monitor
options.D: Sterilizing the handle in a high-heat autoclave

explanation: Great job! You always want to make sure the light is working brightly before the doctor tries to look into the airway. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical healthcare use for a histogram?

options.A: Tracking the exact chronological order of daily nursing shift handovers
options.B: Reviewing patient length of stay to manage bed turnover rates
options.C: Examining patient recovery times in days following major surgery
options.D: Analyzing blood pressure readings across a large outpatient clinic

explanation: Histograms show how often numerical values happen (like blood pressures or days of stay), not the time-order of a daily handover shift. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the special component in fungal cell membranes that antifungal drugs love to target?

options.A: Cellulose
options.B: Peptidoglycan
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Ergosterol

explanation: Fungi use ergosterol in their cell membranes (while humans use cholesterol). This difference lets antifungal drugs attack the fungus without harming human cells! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h2)

question: What is the most crucial detail to write in your nursing notes after a washout?

options.A: The favorite food of the patient's family
options.B: The volume and appearance of the fluid returned
options.C: The weather conditions outside the hospital
options.D: The exact brand name of the lubricant used

explanation: Always document what came out! Recording the amount and look of the return proves that the procedure worked and was safe. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h7)

question: What kind of drug property makes it most likely to build up in breast milk for the baby to absorb?

options.A: A long half-life combined with high lipid solubility
options.B: High protein binding capacity in maternal blood
options.C: Water solubility with a very long elimination time
options.D: Complete destruction by the maternal stomach acid

explanation: Drugs that dissolve easily in fat (lipid-soluble) and hang around in the body a long time (long half-life) tend to linger in breast milk. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h7)

question: What happens to a reflex if the sensory neuron gets damaged or cut?

options.A: Only the integration center will process the signal.
options.B: The brain will take over the reflex function.
options.C: The reflex response will fail to occur.
options.D: The effector will react continuously without stopping.

explanation: Think of a reflex arc like a relay race. If one runner (the sensory neuron) drops out, the message never reaches the finish line and the reflex doesn't happen. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h2)

question: What is the proper way to fix a writing error on a paper nursing chart?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the nursing notes
options.B: Draw a single line through the error and write your initials
options.C: Scratch out the wrong words until they disappear
options.D: Cover the mistake completely with thick correction fluid

explanation: Well done! Drawing a single line keeps the original words readable while showing it was corrected, preventing any look of tampering. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which skin sign strongly points to a liver problem or high bilirubin levels?

options.A: Pallor
options.B: Petechiae
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Jaundice

explanation: Jaundice gives the skin and eyes a yellowish tint because bilirubin is building up in the body. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h6)

question: What kind of muscle makes up the external anal sphincter?

options.A: Smooth muscle
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Skeletal muscle
options.D: Elastic cartilage

explanation: Because the outer sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, you have voluntary control over it. It's what lets you hold it in until you reach a toilet! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: A patient eats a very salty meal. What is their body most likely to do right after?

options.A: Extracellular fluid shifts completely inside the cells
options.B: Thirst increases and the kidneys retain more water
options.C: The kidneys immediately excrete all circulating sodium
options.D: Blood pressure drops rapidly due to sudden dehydration

explanation: Exactly! High salt makes you thirsty and tells your kidneys to hold onto water to keep everything nicely diluted. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of mastitis in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Foul-smelling brownish lochia
options.B: Localized breast redness, pain, and fever
options.C: Complete absence of milk production
options.D: Painless bilateral breast enlargement

explanation: Mastitis means the breast tissue is inflamed or infected. You'll usually spot a painful, red, warm area on the breast along with fever and body aches. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: What advice should a nurse give to help a patient maintain healthy vaginal flora?

options.A: Use scented soaps daily inside the vaginal canal for deep cleaning.
options.B: Wear tight synthetic underwear to keep the area dry.
options.C: Avoid harsh vaginal douches that disrupt protective bacteria.
options.D: Stop taking prescribed antibiotics as soon as itching stops.

explanation: Fantastic! Douching washes away the good bacteria (lactobacilli) and messes with natural pH, making it way easier for bad germs and yeast to take over. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h8)

question: A patient has been convulsing for eight minutes straight without waking up. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Wait quietly at the bedside until the patient stops moving on their own
options.B: Have the patient stand up and walk around to clear their head
options.C: Call for emergency medical help and prepare airway support and rescue medication
options.D: Ask the family members what the patient ate for breakfast

explanation: This is a true emergency! Prolonged seizures cut off vital oxygen to the brain, so you need to sound the alarm and grab rescue medication right away. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h8)

question: What is the best way for a community nurse to stop the spread of diarrhoea in a village?

options.A: Providing mosquito nets for sleeping areas at night
options.B: Teaching proper handwashing with soap and safe water storage
options.C: Inspecting local houses for structural roof damage
options.D: Distributing high-dose antibiotic capsules to all households

explanation: Diarrhoea germs usually spread through the faecal-oral route via dirty hands and water. Simple hygiene education and clean water storage save lives! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h7)

question: What is the main goal of performing CPR on a patient in cardiac arrest?

options.A: To cool down the body and protect the brain
options.B: To clear thick mucus from blocked airways
options.C: To restore normal heart rhythm immediately
options.D: To keep oxygenated blood flowing to vital organs

explanation: CPR acts as an artificial pump to circulate remaining oxygen in the blood to the brain and heart until advanced help arrives. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h1)

question: You see a senior nurse recapping a needle with both hands. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Kindly remind them of the risk and suggest a safer way
options.B: Report them to the police right away
options.C: Ignore it because they have more experience
options.D: Copy them so you can finish your work faster

explanation: Be polite and respectful, but speak up! Friendly peer reminders build a safer, more supportive workplace for everyone. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h8)

question: A patient with a progressive neurological disorder starts having trouble swallowing and controlling their bladder. What do we call this type of issue?

options.A: Acute infection
options.B: Sensory overload
options.C: Autonomic dysfunction
options.D: Cerebellar excitation

explanation: The autonomic nervous system handles automatic body jobs like swallowing, digestion, and bladder control. When it gets impaired, these tricky symptoms show up. You're mastering patient assessment! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h4)

question: You are assisting with a wound wash and fluid is likely to splash. What PPE do you need?

options.A: Gloves and a standard cloth surgical cap only
options.B: Gloves, gown, mask, and eye protection
options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and a paper face mask only
options.D: A heavy rubber apron and heavy-duty utility boots

explanation: Well done! Whenever there's a risk of splashing, you want full protection—hands, body, face, and eyes—to keep yourself safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: How do thyroid hormones affect a person's Basal Metabolic Rate?

options.A: They slow down heart rate to conserve oxygen inside the vital organs
options.B: They regulate water balance to prevent rapid shifts in body weight
options.C: They stimulate fat cells to store extra energy during periods of rest
options.D: They act as the main accelerator for cellular energy use across the body

explanation: Your thyroid gland is like the engine's spark plug. Its hormones control how fast your cells turn nutrients into energy, setting your overall metabolic pace. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h2)

question: What two measurements are used to calculate cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) in the brain?

options.A: Mean arterial pressure and intracranial pressure
options.B: Systolic blood pressure and respiratory rate
options.C: Heart rate and central venous pressure
options.D: Oxygen saturation and core body temperature

explanation: You find the CPP by taking the mean arterial pressure and subtracting the intracranial pressure. You've got this formula down! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h5)

question: In occupational health, what is the FIRST and best line of defense against workplace air hazards?

options.A: Putting up exhaust fans in the work area
options.B: Giving workers certified face masks or respirators
options.C: Rotating shifts so workers spend less time near the hazard
options.D: Completely removing or replacing the dangerous material

explanation: Elimination and substitution are top priorities in safety. If you get rid of the hazard entirely, nobody has to rely on masks or fans to stay safe! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which of the following is part of routine safety monitoring for someone on long-term ARVs?

options.A: Performing a daily chest X-ray to look for bone fractures
options.B: Repeating HIV testing every single week to see if the virus is gone
options.C: Checking kidney and liver function tests regularly alongside clinical screenings
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure only when they report chest pain

explanation: Well done! Since ARVs are processed by the body over years, we run periodic liver and kidney lab tests to catch any organ strain early. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h6)

question: Which piece of equipment is an absolute must to have right at the bedside after major mouth surgery?

options.A: An interactive electronic speech tablet
options.B: Suction equipment and bag-valve-mask device
options.C: Heavy rubber mouth guards
options.D: Warm saline foot bath basins

explanation: Suction keeps the airway clear of blood and saliva, so emergency tools must always be ready to roll. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why might a nurse need to drain a huge, overfilled bladder in stages instead of all at once?

options.A: To ensure the drainage bag does not overflow onto the floor
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling a sudden surge of happiness
options.C: To give the laboratory technicians enough time to test the urine
options.D: To prevent rapid decompression injury and bleeding inside the bladder

explanation: Draining a massive amount of urine too fast can cause the blood vessels inside the bladder wall to burst and bleed. Slow and steady is safer here! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h5)

question: A newborn with a large cephalhematoma is at risk for jaundice. What is the physiological reason for this?

options.A: Breakdown of trapped red blood cells releases bilirubin
options.B: Excessive meconium absorption blocks the bile ducts
options.C: The liver stops working due to the scalp trauma
options.D: Vitamin K injections turn the baby's skin yellow

explanation: As the body reabsorbs the pooled blood from a cephalhematoma, the breakdown of hemoglobin produces excess bilirubin, increasing jaundice risk. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h5)

question: Why might some patients with cervical irritation feel absolutely no symptoms at all?

options.A: The inflammatory process can remain mild and localized without triggering pain receptors.
options.B: Hormones in the vagina completely block any physical sensation of swelling.
options.C: The body instantly neutralizes all bacterial toxins before they reach the surface.
options.D: Nerve endings in the cervix are purely motor and never transmit sensory signals.

explanation: Exactly! Mild inflammation often stays quiet without setting off pain signals, which is why regular screening tests are so important for women's health. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: Which of these is normally NOT needed when creating a standard case definition for a disease?

options.A: The timeframe of symptom onset
options.B: The geographic location of exposure
options.C: The patient's religious affiliation
options.D: Specific physical signs and symptoms

explanation: Disease tracking is about clinical signs, time, and place—a person's religion has nothing to do with how an infection spreads! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h3)

question: During patient assessment, which finding strongly suggests an underlying immune deficiency?

options.A: A sudden increase in energy levels and appetite
options.B: Localized itching from a minor insect bite
options.C: A single episode of mild seasonal influenza
options.D: Recurrent, severe, and unusual infections that do not respond well to standard treatment

explanation: Well done! A healthy body shakes off normal infections easily, but repeated or stubborn infections are a big red flag for immune breakdown. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h6)

question: What makes true sexual consent valid?

options.A: Financial approval from the local community leader
options.B: Written permission signed by both set of parents
options.C: The freedom to say no without negative consequences
options.D: Physical dominance by one partner over the other

explanation: You got it! Consent must always be a free and willing choice, without any force, threats, or pressure. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h4)

question: What must a participant give before answering a research questionnaire?

options.A: Proof of health insurance
options.B: A physician's referral letter
options.C: A notarized identity card
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after being fully informed about the study's purpose. Ethical nursing practice starts here! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: Which government body is mainly responsible for inspecting and licensing assisted living facilities?

options.A: State health or social services departments
options.B: Federal military defense agencies
options.C: International travel and tourism boards
options.D: National automotive safety councils

explanation: State health departments set the rules, run routine checks, and make sure assisted living homes follow health and safety laws. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)

question: Roughly what percentage of waste coming out of healthcare facilities is actually considered hazardous?

options.A: 95 to 100 percent
options.B: 10 to 25 percent
options.C: 75 to 90 percent
options.D: 50 to 60 percent

explanation: Spot on! The vast majority of hospital waste is actually general refuse. Only about 10 to 25 percent requires special hazardous handling. Knowing this helps us manage disposal budgets and safety better! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h1)

question: What is a common misunderstanding about what local disaster agencies do?

options.A: Many believe local agencies possess more aircraft than the national air force
options.B: Citizens assume local agencies are solely responsible for national monetary policy
options.C: People often think they only distribute relief materials after a crisis rather than focusing on prevention
options.D: It is widely assumed that local agencies manage international trade agreements

explanation: Exactly! While handing out relief is the part we see most, good local agencies actually put huge effort into stopping disasters before they happen. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which two drugs are most commonly used together for a medical abortion?

options.A: Oxytocin and ergometrine
options.B: Ampicillin and metronidazole
options.C: Paracetamol and ibuprofen
options.D: Mifepristone and misoprostol

explanation: Great job! Mifepristone pauses the pregnancy, and misoprostol helps the uterus contract and empty safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h4)

question: What is the preferred modern method for clearing the uterus safely during post-abortion care?

options.A: Vaginal douching with hot water
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA)
options.C: High-dose oxytocin infusion alone
options.D: Radical abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: MVA is gentle, quick, and much safer for the uterine wall than old-fashioned sharp scraping (curettage). It's a wonderful modern standard! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h7)

question: What triggers hormone release during humoral stimulation?

options.A: Tropic hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary
options.B: Emotional stress and physical trauma responses
options.C: Changes in ion or nutrient levels in the blood
options.D: Direct electrical impulses sent from the brain

explanation: Humoral stimuli mean the glands are tasting the blood directly—like checking if there is too much sugar or calcium floating around. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is psychological safety so important in healthcare team meetings?

options.A: It guarantees that every meeting will finish exactly on schedule
options.B: It eliminates the need for a formal meeting agenda
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever disagreeing with senior doctors
options.D: It encourages junior staff to speak up about patient safety concerns without fear

explanation: When staff feel safe from harsh judgment, even junior nurses can freely speak up about safety risks. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h4)

question: Which injection route is standard for administering the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine to a newborn?

options.A: Deep intravenous bolus injection into a peripheral vein
options.B: Intramuscular injection into the thigh muscle
options.C: Intradermal injection to create a shallow skin wheal
options.D: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty arm tissue

explanation: BCG is given intradermally into the superficial layers of the skin, typically on the upper arm, producing a characteristic small raised bleb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: Which of the following describes a primary data collection method?

options.A: Reading a published textbook summary of historical mortality rates
options.B: Interviewing patients directly after surgery for a new study
options.C: Downloading a public census file from a government website
options.D: Extracting anonymized blood pressure logs from old hospital archives

explanation: Primary data is gathered firsthand by the researcher specifically to answer their own current research question. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental protection and waste regulations?

options.A: NCC
options.B: NAPTIP
options.C: NESREA
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) is the body making sure environmental laws and waste rules are followed across Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h10)

question: Which specific pelvic joint is most directly affected by symphysis pubis dysfunction?

options.A: The knee hinge joint
options.B: The hip socket joint
options.C: The ankle mortise joint
options.D: The pubic symphysis joint

explanation: Symphysis pubis dysfunction causes pain right at the front pubic joint where the two pelvic bones meet. It's a common area of discomfort! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving recommendations for future research?

options.A: To give graduate students easy thesis topics they do not have to think about
options.B: To guide subsequent studies based on current gaps and unanswered questions
options.C: To prove that the current study answered every single question in nursing
options.D: To ensure the original researcher gets paid for all future grants

explanation: You've got this! No single study answers everything. Pointing out what's left to discover helps the next wave of researchers. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is regular exercise and an active lifestyle good for a patient's bone health?

options.A: Lifestyle habits have no direct connection to skeletal strength
options.B: Weight-bearing exercise stimulates bone density and strengthens supporting muscles
options.C: Sedentary habits automatically increase vitamin D absorption in the skin
options.D: Exercise prevents all forms of genetic joint disease completely

explanation: Exactly right! Putting gentle physical stress on bones through movement tells the body to build stronger, denser bones. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h7)

question: On an ECG machine, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.A: The heart resting and recovering
options.B: Upper chambers squeezing
options.C: Lower chambers relaxing
options.D: Lower chambers electrical activity before they squeeze

explanation: The big tall spike on the ECG screen (the QRS) is the electrical wave racing through the ventricles right before they pump blood out. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main difference between curative treatment and palliative care?

options.A: Curative treatment aims to eradicate disease, while palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life.
options.B: Curative treatment is only for the elderly, while palliative care is for young children.
options.C: Curative treatment ignores physical pain, while palliative care focuses only on surgery.
options.D: Curative treatment is provided at home, while palliative care requires an intensive care unit.

explanation: Think of it this way: curative treatment fights the disease itself to get rid of it, while palliative care fights the discomfort and pain so the patient can feel better day-to-day. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before using a bed accessory on a patient?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to the surface
options.B: Label it with the patient's full home address
options.C: Submerge the entire device in boiling water
options.D: Inspect it for cracks, sharp edges, or loose parts

explanation: Safety first! Always check equipment for any cracks or sharp spots before use to protect your patient from accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: A nurse needs to give an IM vaccine to a healthy adult. Which site is the most appropriate choice?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Abdomen
options.C: Dorsogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: The deltoid muscle is easily accessible and standard for routine adult vaccinations like tetanus or influenza. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: What do we call pain or a burning feeling when passing urine?

options.A: Retention
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Incontinence
options.D: Hematuria

explanation: Dysuria is just the medical word for painful or burning urination. Great term to keep in your clinical vocabulary bag! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h2)

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' mean?

options.A: Providing many vitamins and minerals relative to the calorie count
options.B: Being imported from foreign countries to ensure high quality
options.C: Containing only fats and proteins with zero carbohydrates
options.D: Having high amounts of calories and sugar in a small serving

explanation: Spot on! Nutrient-dense foods pack a heavy punch of vitamins and minerals into every single calorie, giving you the best value for your health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: Why should Nigerian nurses do health education in the community alongside bedside care?

options.A: To fulfill strict legal requirements set by international bodies
options.B: To help demystify cultural myths and educate people on safe reproductive practices
options.C: To replace doctors during hospital strikes and emergencies
options.D: To generate extra revenue for the hospital administration

explanation: Great nurses know healing happens outside the ward too! Community talks help clear up dangerous myths and guide people toward safe practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the medical term for the patchy, purplish skin color that appears on the hands and feet when circulation slows down?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Mottling
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Mottling happens when blood flow slows way down, causing blood to pool in the hands and feet with a purplish, blotchy pattern. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a reliable way for a nurse to assess a patient's overall nutritional status on its own?

options.A: Observing clinical signs such as skin condition and muscle wasting
options.B: Performing anthropometric measurements like height and weight
options.C: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday without any other data
options.D: Reviewing biochemical laboratory values such as serum albumin

explanation: Spot on! A single 24-hour food recall can easily be inaccurate and doesn't give the full clinical picture without physical checks and lab results. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h7)

question: What is a nurse's legal and ethical duty regarding a client's family planning records?

options.A: Post the details on community bulletin boards for public awareness
options.B: Maintain strict confidentiality and protect records from unauthorized viewers
options.C: Share the client's medical history openly with any curious neighbors
options.D: Hand over all clinical notes to the client's extended family members

explanation: Confidentiality protects the client's privacy, ensuring their health information is only shared with authorized medical personnel involved in their direct care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the Safe Motherhood Initiative?

options.A: To promote exclusive formula feeding
options.B: To increase the national birth rate
options.C: To reduce maternal mortality and morbidity
options.D: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants

explanation: You've got this! The Safe Motherhood framework was set up specifically to lower the rates of death and severe illness linked to pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: When is a formative evaluation carried out during a health education program?

question: What is a direct consequence of having weak vital data collection systems in a country?

question: Why can a sudden infection or severe physical stress cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

question: During suctioning, your patient's oxygen saturation drops rapidly and their heart rate becomes irregular. What is your very first action?

question: Which food must be strictly avoided by a patient taking a Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)?

question: Why is tracking the baby's heartbeat so crucial when a mum is feeling distressed?

question: Where is medication placed when using the sublingual route?

question: What major nutrient do legumes like cowpeas (beans) and bambara groundnuts bring to our local pots?

question: When leaving an isolation room, what is the very first piece of PPE you take off?

question: Why must food be digested before your body can absorb it?

options.A: Digestion adds essential vitamins that trigger active transport

question: A patient with a back injury to the vertebrae has damage in which body cavity?

options.D: Spinal cavity

question: How do poverty and transport delays worsen severe maternal illness in local communities?

options.C: They lower the normal blood pressure of the mother below safe levels

question: A patient is scared to name their coworkers because they are worried about losing their job. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Threaten to report the patient to the local police force for withholding data
options.B: Assure the patient of strict confidentiality and explain the public health goal
options.C: Tell the employer immediately so other workers can be screened by force

question: How does the body respond during a negative energy balance?

options.C: It increases total body mass rapidly.

question: Why is it helpful to give a client a written appointment card after her injection?

question: You are alone with a patient having a severe drug reaction. After stopping the IV, what should you do next?

options.C: Call for emergency help while staying with the patient

question: Which condition is a major safety risk specifically related to maternity care?

explanation: Excessive bleeding after childbirth is one of the leading preventable causes of maternal mortality worldwide, requiring strict monitoring and rapid response. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why would a doctor order a stool culture for a patient with ongoing diarrhoea?

options.C: To check for hidden microscopic blood in the stool

question: What is the main problem that causes most cases of peripheral arterial disease (PAD)?

options.D: Fatty plaque building up and narrowing the arteries

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand a patient's cultural background regarding health?

options.A: Culture completely prevents patients from experiencing chronic pain.

options.C: Culture determines the exact medical dosage a patient's liver can metabolize.

question: A coal miner has a chronic cough and trouble breathing after years underground. What caused this?

options.A: Inhalation and accumulation of dust particles in lung tissue
options.B: Bacterial infection spreading rapidly through the crowded workshop
options.C: Severe vitamin deficiency caused by working long shifts in the dark

question: A patient asks what happens to sperm immediately after they are created in the seminiferous tubules. What is the best nursing response?

question: Why can relying only on 'the way we've always done it' (clinical tradition) be tricky in healthcare?

options.A: It prevents nurses from communicating effectively with doctors

question: What is the very first thing you should do when preparing a client for a family planning referral?

question: How do restrictive lung disorders mainly affect how the lungs work?

question: A patient has overdosed on an opioid. Which signs would you expect to see on assessment?

options.B: Excessive sweating and muscle twitching
options.C: Pinpoint pupils and slow breathing
options.D: Rapid heart rate and dilated pupils

question: What is the golden rule right after using a disposable injection needle?

question: What is the main job of our respiratory system?

options.D: Filtering bacteria out of the bloodstream

question: What is the term for physical pregnancy symptoms, like nausea, that are sometimes experienced by expectant fathers?

question: Which specific cells in the testes are responsible for making testosterone?

question: What is a primary assessment tool used during a home prenatal visit to check fetal well-being?

question: What is one of the most important roles of a nurse in a pediatric care team?

question: How does the work differ between a Senior CHEW and a Junior CHEW?

question: Why must certain dangerous illnesses like yellow fever be reported immediately to national authorities?

question: What happens in a vestibular hair cell when its hairs bend toward the tallest one (the kinocilium)?

question: Why should nurses encourage patients to use adaptive tools during ADLs?

question: What does a simple pulse oximeter clip measure on a patient's finger?

question: A nurse notices the clinic frequently runs out of safety boxes, causing staff to leave used needles on trays. What is the best action to take?

question: What is the main focus of a community diagnosis?

question: Why is a risk assessment done before holding a mass gathering?

question: During a neuro exam, why do nurses check different parts of the body instead of just the head?

question: Oops! A scrubbed nurse accidentally drops their hands below waist level before putting on a gown. What should they do?

question: A family caregiver looks totally exhausted and says they can't handle daily wound care anymore. What should you do first?

question: Which enzyme in your saliva starts breaking down carbohydrates right in your mouth?

question: A patient asks why their urine culture takes up to 48 hours while a dipstick takes minutes. What is the best way to explain this?

question: Why should you never point a used sharp device toward your own body?

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient who has recovered from serum sickness before they leave the hospital?

question: How do the results of an MBO performance review affect the future?

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood programs?

question: You are getting ready to give IV phenytoin to a patient. Which IV fluid should you use to flush and dilute it?

question: What do we call the signs of pregnancy that are felt and reported only by the mother herself?

question: What is the primary purpose of the sutures and fontanelles in a foetal skull?

question: A patient with gestational diabetes asks what diet changes to make. What should you suggest?

question: Which phase of the ovarian cycle always stays pretty much the same length for most women?

question: How does chloride rushing into brain cells help calm the nervous system?

question: Which factor is most important when deciding if a medicine belongs on an essential drug list?
